questions.markdown: Compute the 6-point DFT of the sequence $x(n)=\{0,1,2,3,2,1\}$ using matrix multiplication method.
State and prove the circular convolution property of DFT of two sequences $x_1(n)$ and $x_2(n)$.
Describe the Goertzel algorithm with expressions. What is it used for?

Compute the 8-point DFT of the sequence $x(n)=\{1,0.5,0,-0.5,-1,-0.5,0,0.5\}$ using decimation in frequency FFT algorithm. Illustrate that the computation is faster than the direct computation of DFT.
Analyze the FIR lattice structure whose lattice coefficients are: $K_1=0.65$, $K_2=-0.34$ & $K_3=0.8$, and obtain its impulse response coefficients.
Realize the linear phase FIR filter of length $M=7$, whose first four filter coefficients are: $1$, $1/3$, $-1/8$ and $1/5$.

A LPF has the desired frequency response

$$
|H_d(e^{j\omega})|=\begin{cases}
1, & 0\le |\omega|\le 0.5\pi \\
0, & elsewhere
\end{cases}
$$

Determine the filter coefficients $h(n)$ using frequency sampling technique. Assume filter length $M=9$.
Determine the unit sample response $h(n)$ of a 4 length linear phase symmetric FIR filter having frequency response $H_r(0)=1$ and $H_r(\pi/2)=0.5$.
From Q3B determine the system function $H(z)$ and the phase $\phi(\omega)$ for $H_r(\omega)>0$.

Certain IIR Butterworth LPF has the following specifications

$$
-1.5\,\text{dB} \le 20\log_{10}(|H(e^{j\omega})|) \le 0\,\text{dB},\quad 0\le \omega \le \pi/3
$$

$$
20\log_{10}(|H(e^{j\omega})|) \le -10\,\text{dB},\quad 0.5\pi \le \omega \le \pi
$$

Assume $T=1$ second. Obtain the prewarped analog edge frequency specifications, order of filter, 3-dB cut-off frequency and poles of the filter.

$$
H(z)=\frac{1+z^{-1}+0.5z^{-2}}{1+0.2z^{-1}-0.15z^{-2}}
$$

Obtain the lattice ladder structure.

Convert the analog filter into its equivalent digital filter using impulse invariance method whose transfer function is given by

$$
H(s)=\frac{s+1}{s^2+2s+17}
$$

Assume $T=1$ second.
Illustrate the concept of spectral leakage and spectral resolution problems occurring in spectral estimation from finite duration signals.
